why: Asks probability of selecting a white button from entire bag. Denominator is total buttons (whole group), no restriction. Direct ratio of favorable to total.
Asks probability of selecting a negative number from a 3-element data set. Denominator is 3 (whole group). Direct count-to-total ratio.
Asks probability of selecting a blue house from all houses on the street. Denominator is total houses (whole group). Direct ratio.

Probability 0.35 is given; unknown is the count of blue marbles. Solve: 0.35 × 60 = 21. PRB.7 because probability is given and count is unknown. C (35) confuses decimal with count; D (39) computes complement 60−21.
Asks probability of selecting a defective bead from total production. Denominator is whole batch (whole group). May require simplifying the fraction (canceling common factor).
Asks probability of selecting a positive number from a 3-element data set. Denominator is 3 (whole group). Direct ratio.

Two-way table (age × visits). Asks probability of selecting a customer at least N years old from all customers. Denominator is grand total (whole group). Requires locating the marginal total for the age row and dividing by grand total.

One-way frequency table of gemstone classifications. Asks probability of selecting color Y from all gemstones. Denominator is total gemstones (whole group). Read frequency from table, divide by total.
Asks probability of nonfiction book from total n+12 books. Denominator is whole bookshelf (whole group). Answer is n/(n+12), requiring algebraic expression of probability. No restriction phrase.
4 defective out of 1000. P = 4/1000 = 0.004. Denominator is 1000 (whole group). Requires decimal conversion. B (0.04) uses wrong power of 10; C (0.4) divides by 10; D (4) treats count as probability.
Asks probability of selecting a saxophone player from entire band. Denominator is total band members (whole group). Direct ratio.
Two-way table (texting × phone use) with 799 teens. Asks probability of talking on cell phone daily from all 799. Denominator is 799 (whole group). Read column marginal 415 and divide by 799.
Two-way table (location × age). Asks probability of at least N years old from all members. Denominator is total members (whole group). Read age-row marginal and divide by grand total.
4 rocky out of 8 planets. P = 4/8 = 1/2. Denominator is 8 (whole group). Requires reducing fraction to lowest terms.
One-way frequency table (rock classification). Asks probability of igneous from all rocks. Denominator is total rocks (whole group). Read frequency and divide by total.
Two-way table (grade × mascot). Asks probability of lion vote from all students. Denominator is grand total (whole group). Sum lion row across grades, divide by total, reduce fraction.

Asks 'How many males do not play a school sport?' — a count, not a probability. No probability is given or asked for. Student reads/computes a cell value from the two-way table. Fits OVD.6 (read or interpret a data display), not any PRB sub-skill.

One-way table: 10 baritones out of 25. P = 10/25 = 0.40. Denominator is 25 (whole group). Convert to decimal. A (0.10) misreads count as decimal; C (0.60) uses complement 15/25; D (0.67) uses wrong denominator.

'Of the students who completed a summer internship in 2010' restricts to 2010 column. Denominator is 2010 total (140), not grand total. Fraction = Valley 2010 (65) / 140. Restriction phrase triggers PRB.6.
Two-way table (gasoline × beverage) with 135 customers. Asks probability of not purchasing gasoline from all 135 customers. Denominator is 135 (whole group). P = 50/135. No restriction phrase.
One-way table of marble colors. 10 blue out of 40 total. P = 10/40 = 1/4. Denominator is 40 (whole group). Direct ratio from frequency table.
Fair die with labeled faces. Probability of rolling a specific number = 1/(number of faces). Denominator is total faces (whole group). Direct ratio.

Two-way table (car type × price). Asks probability of hybrid AND ≤$25k from all 14 cars. Denominator is 14 (grand total, whole group). Read joint cell = 2, P = 2/14 = 1/7. No restriction — both conditions define the event, not a restricted sample space.

'What fraction of the chocolate-colored kittens has deep blue eyes?' — 'of the chocolate-colored kittens' restricts to chocolate row. Denominator is 16 (chocolate total), not 48. Fraction = 12/16 = 3/4. PRB.6.
Two-way table (camping × bicycle). Asks probability of camping AND no bicycle from all state parks. Denominator is total parks 20+5+8+4 = 37 (whole group). Read joint cell = 5, P = 5/37.

Asks probability of 'neither blue nor yellow' from all cubes. Denominator is total cubes (whole group). Student must merge red+white categories (complement of blue+yellow). Multi-step counting with category merging.

Total customers and probabilities for theaters A and B are given. Unknown is count in theater C. Solve: C = total − (P_A × total) − (P_B × total). Probability given, count unknown — PRB.7. Requires complement reasoning.
N-sided polygon, one vertex selected at random. P = 1/N. Denominator is total vertices (whole group). Direct ratio. Free-response decimal/fraction.

'If one of the days on which there was no rain is selected at random' restricts to no-rain days. Denominator is 64 (no-rain total), not 84. P(weekend | no rain) = 16/64 = 1/4. Restriction phrase triggers PRB.6.
Total attendees and probabilities for groups A and B are given. Unknown is count in group C. Same structure as 1fc4f47b: probability given, count unknown. Requires complement reasoning.
1200/day × 5 days = 6000 accounts in first 5 days. Fraction = 6000/60000 = 1/10. Denominator is 60000 (whole group). Requires multiplying rate by time, then forming ratio. No restriction phrase.
'Of those presidents who were at least 50 years old' restricts to ages 50+. Denominator = 13+11+7+3 = 34. Numerator (≥60) = 7+3 = 10. Fraction = 10/34 = 5/17. Must merge age categories ≥50 and ≥60.

A fraction of total female population is given. Student computes target count = fraction × 180, then compares each type's female count. Chinstrap (59) is closest to the target. Probability/fraction given, count is the unknown — PRB.7.
Box with red and blue pens. Probability of red = red/(red+blue). Denominator is total pens (whole group). Direct ratio. Free-response.
'If the person chosen works in the Human Resources department' restricts to HR. Denominator is HR total = 4+2 = 6. P(master's | HR) = 2/6 = 1/3. Restriction phrase triggers PRB.6.
Two-way table (color × shape). Asks probability of red tile from all tiles. Denominator is grand total (whole group). Sum red column and divide by total. Free-response.

'given that the participant is at least 10 years of age' — explicit 'given that' restricts to ≥10. Denominator is sum of age groups ≥10 (not grand total). Must merge age categories, then compute P(group A | ≥10).
'given that the flower is a tulip' — explicit 'given that' restricts to tulip row. Denominator is tulip total, not grand total. P(site A | tulip). Free-response.

'of states with a state-level sales tax' restricts to sales-tax states. Denominator = 39+6 = 45. 6/45 ≈ 13.3%. Must identify correct base quantity and convert to percent. A (6.0%) uses 100 as denominator; B (12.0%) uses 50.
'given that the participant is at least N years of age' — explicit 'given that' restricts to age subset. Must merge age categories at or above threshold, then compute P(group A | ≥N). Free-response.
P(MTN) = 0.43 and total = 97 million are given. p = 0.43 × 97 ≈ 41.71 → 42 million. Probability given, count unknown — PRB.7. Free-response integer.
'given that the tree is N feet or taller' — explicit 'given that' restricts to tall trees. Denominator is total trees ≥N feet (not all trees). P(maple | ≥N feet). PRB.6.

'who is rhesus negative' restricts to Rh− row (PRB.6). Within that restriction, P(B | Rh−) is given and x (a count in the table) is unknown. Student sets up 2/(10+x) = given fraction and solves algebraically for x (PRB.7). Requires clearing fractions and restricting to condition's row.
